title: Efficient ILT via Multigrid-Schwartz Method
problem: Inverse Lithography Technology (ILT) is computationally expensive for large-scale chip layouts, and partitioning into tiles introduces discontinuities at tile boundaries that can cause manufacturing defects.
motivation: ILT is critical for advanced chip manufacturing as an important Resolution Enhancement Technology.
method: The approach applies multigrid-Schwarz domain decomposition to solve tile assembly problems in ILT. The Schwarz method iteratively refines solutions at tile interfaces to eliminate stitching discontinuities, enabling parallel processing while maintaining quality comparable to full-chip ILT.
key_novelty: Using multigrid-Schwarz domain decomposition to overcome tile assembly discontinuities in ILT, providing an alternative to traditional divide-and-conquer approaches.
contributions: Multigrid-Schwarz method for tile-based ILT assembly
Elimination of tile stitching discontinuities preventing manufacturing failures
Achieves comparable performance to full-chip ILT with improved parallelizability
Demonstrates parallel speedup over sequential processing

metrics.speedup: parallel speedup achieved in parallel mode

primary_theme: Tile-based lithography optimization via domain decomposition
